title: Capstone: Your Full AI-Powered Dev Environment

sections.content:
## What You'll Build

A complete, documented description of your personal AI development environment — everything working, everything verified, everything written down so that you (or someone else) could rebuild it from scratch.

This isn't just documentation. The act of walking through every component and confirming it works will likely reveal a few things that got half-configured along the way. Fix them now, while you have the focus.

**The output of this capstone is `notes/my-ai-dev-environment.md`** — a setup document that represents the cumulative result of 14 parts. If you had to start over on a new machine, this file tells you exactly what to install and how to configure it.

sections.title: Audit and Document Your Full AI Setup
sections.content:
## The Checklist

Work through each component. For each one: test that it works, then document it.

---

**Component 1 — VS Code Setup**

Open VS Code. Verify:
- [ ] VS Code is installed and up to date (Help → Check for Updates)
- [ ] These extensions are installed and working: Live Server, Prettier, GitLens, GitHub Copilot (or Continue.dev), at least one AI coding assistant
- [ ] Your settings.json has your preferred font size, auto-save, word wrap, format on save
- [ ] You know how to open the Command Palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P`)

For each installed extension, write one sentence in your document: what it does and why you use it.

---

**Component 2 — Claude Code Configuration**

Open a terminal and type `claude --version` to confirm Claude Code is installed.

Then verify:
- [ ] `claude` launches successfully
- [ ] `/mcp` shows at least 3 connected MCP servers
- [ ] Your CLAUDE.md file exists in `ai-course-projects/` and contains useful instructions
- [ ] At least 2 custom slash commands exist in `.claude/commands/`
- [ ] Your memory file at `~/.claude/memory/` contains your preferences
- [ ] Your user-level settings at `~/.claude/settings.json` are configured correctly

For each MCP server listed by `/mcp`, write one sentence: what it does and when you use it.

---

**Component 3 — Local AI**

Verify:
- [ ] Ollama is installed: `ollama --version`
- [ ] At least one model is downloaded: `ollama list`
- [ ] The Ollama API is responsive: open browser to `http://localhost:11434`
- [ ] Continue.dev in VS Code is configured to use the local model
- [ ] OR: LM Studio is installed with a model loaded

Note which model(s) you have and what you use each one for.

---

**Component 4 — Git and GitHub**

Verify:
- [ ] `git --version` works
- [ ] `git config --global user.name` returns your name
- [ ] `git config --global user.email` returns your email
- [ ] Your `ai-course-projects` folder has at least one commit in its history
- [ ] The GitHub MCP server in Claude Code can list repos from your account

---

**Component 5 — Automations Running**

Verify:
- [ ] At least one n8n workflow is active (the email drafting workflow from 14-3, or automations from 10-2)
- [ ] You know where to find your n8n instance and how to deactivate workflows if needed

List each active automation: what it does and when it runs.

---

**Component 6 — API Access**

Verify:
- [ ] Anthropic API key is in `exercises/.env`
- [ ] `.env` is in `.gitignore`
- [ ] `python exercises/hello-claude.py` still works
- [ ] Spending limits are set in the Anthropic Console

List every service where you have API access (just the service name, not the keys).

---

## Writing the Environment Document

Create `notes/my-ai-dev-environment.md`. Use this structure:

```markdown

|-----------|----------|
| Live Server | Preview HTML with auto-reload |
| Prettier | Auto-format code on save |
| GitLens | Git blame and history inline |
| [your AI extension] | [what it does for you] |
| [continue the list] | |

### Key Settings
Settings.json lives at: [path]
Key customizations: [describe what you changed from defaults]

---

## Claude Code

[claude --version output]

### Active MCP Servers
| Server | What It Does | When I Use It |

| filesystem | Read/write project files | All coding sessions |
| github | Issues, PRs, repo navigation | When working with GitHub |
| [your others] | | |

### Custom Slash Commands

| /review | Reviews file for bugs and readability |
| [others] | |

### CLAUDE.md Approach
[Describe what you put in your project CLAUDE.md files]

[Path to your preferences file]

---

## Local AI

### Ollama
Installed: yes/no
Models: [list with what you use each for]
Connected to: Continue.dev / Claude Code / both

### LM Studio
Installed: yes/no
Primary use: [when you open it]

---

## Automations

### Active n8n Workflows
| Workflow | What It Does | Schedule |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| Email Reply Drafting | Drafts replies to labeled emails | Every 1 min |
| [others from lesson 10-2] | | |

---

## APIs and Credentials

- Anthropic (Claude API)
- GitHub
- [others]

Keys are stored in: [.env files / environment variables / etc.]
Spending limit set: yes/no

---

## My Daily AI Workflow

[Paste your workflow from notes/my-ai-workflow.md — or write it fresh]

---

## Prompt Library

Location: [path to your prompt library from lesson 3-8]

---

- Portfolio: https://[yourusername].github.io
- [Other things you built]

---

## What I'd Set Up First on a New Machine

1. Install VS Code with these extensions: [list]
2. Install Node.js, then Claude Code
3. Install Git and configure user.name/email
4. Install Ollama and pull [model]
5. Copy .claude/settings.json with MCP configs
6. Set up .env with API keys
7. Activate n8n workflows
```

---

## Fixing What's Broken

As you work through the checklist, you'll probably find at least one thing that isn't configured correctly — an MCP server that stopped connecting, a workflow that was deactivated, an extension that needs updating.

Fix those things now. Use Claude Code to help:

```
claude
```

Then: "I'm auditing my setup. When I run `/mcp`, the [server name] server isn't connecting. Here's the error: [paste error]. What's wrong?"

This is exactly what Claude Code is good at. It can read your settings.json, suggest fixes, and test them.

**Share this document.** If you ever join a team, collaborate with a developer, or want to show an employer what your setup looks like — this document says more about your capabilities than a resume line that says "familiar with AI tools." It's specific, verifiable, and shows you built things.
**Capstone 14-4 complete.** Your AI development environment is fully documented. One capstone remains — the open one, where you build something of your own choosing.
